Looping in technical details — I pulled the perf snapshots and live traces (see attached partial logs). Early observations:

- Correlation with catalog refresh: yes. A mapping change in the model catalog (catalog version 20270803-08:00) caused a percentage of requests to be routed to a quantized model variant (q4_1) that uses an experimental kernel path on our runtime. That kernel has significantly higher tail latency for the long-tail sequence lengths (512-2048) used by Continental's queries.
- Metrics: p50 unchanged (~180ms), p95 averaged ~1.1s, p99 spikes to 2.9s for the affected variant; GPU utilization per-instance increased ~12% but not saturated — suggests suboptimal kernel dispatch rather than capacity exhaustion.
- Repro: I reproduced locally by replaying the sample request IDs and toggling the model_variant flag; the q4_1 path reproduces the tail latency.

Immediate remediation options (ranked):
1) Roll back catalog mapping for the affected model ID to force the non-quantized variant (fast path). This is lowest risk and fastest (ETA ~15–25 mins to rollback + validation).
2) Apply a routing rule to blackhole the q4_1 variant for Continental's account until we push a kernel fix (ETA ~1–2 hours).
3) If rollback is not acceptable for policy reasons, we can hotfix runtime kernel config but that is riskier and will take longer.

I'll proceed with option (1) pending sign-off from Kimberly (account) and Marissa (support/ops). I've linked the internal Grafana panel and opened JIRA-OPS-1129 to track the kernel fix. Logs attached: continental_catalog_sync.log.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Hi Alice —

First, apologies for the disruption. We completed a targeted rollback of the catalog mapping for the affected model variant at 08:45 PDT and have validated p95/p99 metrics are returning to baseline for your production traffic. The rollback took ~22 minutes including validation.

What we did:
- Rolled catalog mapping back to the previous stable model variant for the model_id:M-vec-77
- Throttled routing to the q4_1 variant for Continental while we finish a kernel-level fix (JIRA-OPS-1129).
- Issued an internal playbook to avoid automatic promotion of experimental kernel paths in next catalogs for accounts with long-tail sequences.

Customer-facing next steps:
- We will provide a full post-incident report by EOD tomorrow (Aug 5) with timeline, root cause, and permanent remediation plan.
